:::{#def-nb-reg}
#### Negative binomial regression model

A **negative binomial regression model** for a count outcome $Y$
with covariate vector $\vX$ and exposure magnitude $T$
assumes that,
given $\vX = \vx$ and $T = t$,
$Y$ has a [negative binomial distribution](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/distributions.html#def-nb)
with the same mean function as the [Poisson regression model](#def-poisson-reg),

$$\E{Y \mid \vX = \vx, T = t} = \mu(\vx, t) \eqdef t \expf{\eta(\vx)}$$

and with variance

$$\Var{Y \mid \vX = \vx, T = t} = \mu(\vx, t) + \frac{\mu(\vx, t)^2}{\rho}$$ {#eq-nb-reg-var}

for an overdispersion parameter $\rho > 0$
that does not depend on $\vx$ or $t$.

:::
